title: Match on resolved module identity, not specifier strings
note: Both T93 bypasses closed. Relative import (../../../lib/prisma) and barrel re-export now block; the clean control still passes; external suite 7/7 with ZERO baseline drift, so no overshoot.
evidence: The plan premise was partly wrong and the real defect was in a different place. Tracing it: (1) the engine graph matcher was never even called during a check - no debug output at all; (2) the deciding logic is a CLI-side PRE-FILTER, graphImportResolvesToForbidden, which had the identical defect - isForbiddenImport(resolvedPath, forbiddenImports) compares a resolved file path against specifiers; (3) even after fixing that, the engine receives a graph SCOPED TO THE CHANGED FILES, so it cannot derive what @/lib/prisma means - the imports establishing that live outside the diff; (4) MODULE_REEXPORTS_MODULE was not in the kept-edge list, so the barrel chain never reached the engine.
diagnosis: Fix is in four parts: CLI computes forbidden module identities from the FULL graph before scoping; passes them to the engine as matcher.forbidden_module_files; the engine prefers supplied identities and still derives locally for whole-repo checks; and re-export edges are kept in the scoped graph. Also found and recorded a fixture defect: my own T93 fixtures did not reproduce the bypass - inference learned the relative specifier in one and inferred nothing in the other. The scenario only reproduces when the contract learns the alias form from legitimate usage first, and it needs a tsconfig paths mapping, without which the resolver produces 1 resolved edge out of 64 imports.
